definition: Add the values of the signs. IIII is 1 + 1 + 1 + 1.
Take a smaller value away from a larger one. In IV, I before V gives 5 − 1 = 4.
A bar above a numeral. In the thousands convention, X̅ stands for 10,000. A similar bar can mark a numeral without changing its value.
Large-number signs built from I, C and a reversed C. CIↃ means 1,000 and IↃ means 500.
A short upright stroke in handwriting. Two strokes could look like either ii or n, depending on the hand.
A score is twenty. Four scores are eighty. A small superscript xx can mark multiplication by twenty.
A phrase whose selected numeral letters add up to a number, often a year. Capitals can mark which letters to count.
A year number from 1 to 15 in a repeating dating cycle. The same number recurs every fifteen years.
Ab urbe condita, “from the founding of the city”. This reckoning counts from Rome’s traditional foundation in 753 BCE.
A year count used in parts of medieval Iberia. Its year 1 corresponds to 38 BCE.
A line over a numeral that marks it off from nearby writing without multiplying it.
A small raised sign that multiplies the numeral before it. In iiᶜ, the raised c gives 2 × 100.
A j used for i at the end of a numeral. In viij, j adds one, just as in viii.
